name: Sample Liquid Fund A
summary: Lends money to the government and big companies for a few weeks at a time. Your money stays fairly steady. Good for parking money you may need soon.

name: Sample Liquid Fund B
summary: Holds very short loans that are repaid within about three months. Value moves very little day to day. Easy to take money out.

name: Sample Short-Term Debt Fund C
summary: Lends money for one to three years to stable borrowers. A little more movement than a liquid fund. Suits money needed in six months or more.

name: Sample Hybrid Fund A
summary: Splits money between company shares and safer loans. The mix softens big swings. A middle path for a few years.

name: Sample Balanced Fund B
summary: Keeps roughly half in shares and half in loans, and rebalances on its own. Ups and downs are milder than a pure share fund.

name: Sample Conservative Hybrid C
summary: Mostly safer loans with a small slice of shares. Moves gently. Suits someone easing in.

name: Sample Nifty 50 Index Fund A
summary: Buys the same 50 large Indian companies in the Nifty 50 list. No one picks stocks, so costs are low. Value can swing a lot year to year.

name: Sample Sensex Index Fund B
summary: Copies the 30 companies in the Sensex list. Simple and low cost. Needs years to ride out the bumps.

name: Sample Next 50 Index Fund C
summary: Copies the next 50 companies after the biggest ones. Bigger swings than a Nifty 50 fund. For long, patient money.

name: Sample Flexi Cap Fund A
summary: A manager picks shares of small, mid and large companies. Can move sharply up or down. Needs five years or more.

name: Sample Flexi Cap Fund B
summary: Spreads money across companies of all sizes based on the manager's view. Value can fall for long stretches.

name: Sample Flexi Cap Fund C
summary: Actively managed share fund with a wide choice of companies. Higher cost because people choose the shares.

name: Sample Tax Saver (ELSS) Fund A
summary: A share fund that can lower your income tax under old tax rules. Your money is locked for 3 years. Value can swing a lot.

name: Sample Tax Saver (ELSS) Fund B
summary: Invests in company shares with a 3-year lock. Each monthly instalment is locked for its own 3 years.

name: Sample Tax Saver (ELSS) Fund C
summary: Tax-saving share fund run by a manager. You cannot withdraw for 3 years, even in an emergency.

name: Sample Gold Fund A
summary: Follows the price of gold without you storing any. Gold often moves differently from shares. Can stay flat for years.

name: Sample Gold Fund B
summary: Holds units that track gold prices. No locker, no purity worries. Price depends on world markets and the rupee.

name: Sample Gold Savings Fund C
summary: Lets you put small monthly amounts into gold. Value goes up and down with the gold price.
